findings.explanation: The module root has no terraform { required_providers { ... } } block anywhere (main.tf is a placeholder comment). Only the example under example/examplea pins an exact google provider version (7.30.0). Consumers of this module have no signal about which provider versions it was built and tested against, so a caller could resolve an incompatible (too old or too new) google provider version and get plan/apply behaviour that differs from what this module was validated with.
findings.title: Root module declares no required_providers / required_version constraint

findings.explanation: mw_day defaults to 1 (Monday) and mw_hour defaults to 12 (noon UTC). Noon UTC overlaps business hours across most of Europe and the UK, and even a REGIONAL (HA) instance takes a brief failover hit during maintenance. Callers who don't override these defaults get maintenance scheduled during a plausible peak-traffic window rather than an off-hours slot.
findings.remediation: Default to a low-traffic slot, e.g. Sunday early morning UTC: mw_day = 7, mw_hour = 6. Callers in a specific timezone can still override both.
findings.title: Default maintenance window falls in business hours (Monday 12:00 UTC)
